summary: New box Preterit Intransitive: example for sense 2 in Preterit Intransitive (JTM 3.1/8)

data.turoyo: Aḥna stene, uno stene, hama uno qamayto, laṣyono hawxa, qm u syoġo, qm u ṭəlolo dak karme. Fayətina, fayətina, aydarbo saymina annaqla?
data.translation: Und wir, und auch ich, ich als erste duckte mich so an der Mauer, im Schatten der Weinberge. Wir gingen nach und nach vorbei. Was sollten wir jetzt machen?

rationale: First example of protective-concealment sense 2 and new Preterit Intransitive box; 1sg.f state form, morphology provisional.

summary: New box Preterit Intransitive: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (JTM 5.2/42)

data.turoyo: komər i naqqa d azzən, hani azzən laṣən aʕlayye, mərre harke gədoṯən, kəla i farše di ṣluṯo, kələn harke gədoṯən gədmṣalən w aḥna gəquṭlinalle harke.
data.translation: Als sie sich auf den Weg machten, gingen (ihre Gegner) und lauerten ihnen auf. Sie sagten: Sie werden hierher kommen, hier ist die Felsenplatte für das Gebet, hierher werden sie kommen und beten, und wir werden sie hier töten.

rationale: New Preterit Intransitive box; 3pl laṣən and explicit hostile purpose with ʕal-marked target.

data.turoyo: Laṣən di qriṯo qm u zoġo, əmmi: "Ak kəṯoṯayḏan lə kmibayni."
data.translation: Die Bauern lauerten aber dem Hahn auf; denn sie sagten: "Unsre Hühner sind verschwunden";

rationale: New Preterit Intransitive box; independent PrS attestation with qm-target contrasts with aʕlayye.

summary: Preserve lṣele/loṣe and the reported alternative laṣi/loṣe. laṣən in independent JTM and PrS sources supports a Preterit Intransitive box alongside the inherited L-series base form.
Hostile target is marked by ʕal- (JTM 5.2/42; MAC Hanna Dewo/111; PrS 73/72) or qm- (PrS 73/71). In JTM 3.1/8 qm marks location at the wall/shadow, not an animate target.

Protective concealment is accepted as I.2 on one context, without making German crouching posture an independent lexical component. The action noun/look forms do not imply a new “watch over for care” meaning.
Lookup of lṣy 2 shows III malṣele/malṣe with an overt trap object. None of these I forms has that construction; no refile to lṣy 2 is justified.

PrS 73/72 repeats the preceding ambush episode with guns; the selected preceding qm-target and independent ʕal-target examples are sufficient. 58/18 is already quoted; MAC Hanna Dewo/111 is the inherited HD 82 item.
The inherited Participle label and the incomplete gloss Herde are retained as source editorial material, not silently standardized. New labels use the protocol’s exact terminology.

Jan 1.50/2445 extends the already inherited animal-target pattern to mole hunting. aʕle marks the awaited target; baiting and the subsequent knife/killing supply the hostile purpose. Infectum-wa occurs in a habitual sequence.

Jan 2.14/3403 has plural laṣye with separate wən and aʕle; this supports a continuing state of waiting. New material uses Part act.; the inherited heading Participle and its one example are preserved. These are corresponding labels for counting, not two newly distinguished forms.

Jan 2.4/865 has uncomplemented luṣewo in Uṯewo luṣewo kuraxwo after a military-administration context. Hostility, a concrete target and a technical inspection meaning are not explicit. The machine translation inspect is insufficient to widen sense 1.
No Jan token independently supports or changes round-1 sense 2. No light-verb collocation is established.
JTM 3.1/8 laṣyono: confirm feminine Preterit Intransitive versus a Part act. plus person predication; does the verb lexicalize concealment or specifically bodily crouching?

MAC Hanna Dewo/111 versus embedded HD 82: are these distinct edition/transcription numbering systems? The exact quotation is identified, so a modern structured source is added without deleting the old marker.
The inherited Participle example láṣyene has only the gloss Herde for qaṭʕo, not a full translation. No supplied occurrence licenses reconstructing its full translation.

Jan 2.4/865: does luṣewo mean looking around/monitoring without hostile intent, or concealed watching? Confirm before broadening sense 1 or adding a separate sense. The English inspect is machine translation.
Confirm that inherited láṣyene and Jan laṣye wən belong to the same Part act. predication despite the different written copula placement. The inherited Participle heading is retained.
